capabilities.target: payments-agent (pay chosen vendor from bank details in task)

inputs.source: Employee purchase request submitted via SSO-authenticated internal system
Vendor quote emails and attachments from external senders

instructions.note: The prompt asserts 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but runtime notes state payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task with no further verification. The claimed downstream safety check does not exist in the actual design.

The instruction 'Use the bank details from the chosen quote' gives the content of an untrusted, externally supplied vendor quote direct authority to set the payment destination, with no requirement to verify it against a trusted vendor record.
'Choose the best one' gives no objective criteria for vendor selection, leaving the decision open to manipulation by an attacker-crafted quote engineered to appear most attractive.

The design's single approval step authorizes only the item and budget before any quote exists, and its record is not passed to payments-agent, so no approval gate actually covers cap.delegate_payment. Autonomy is scored as A3 for this capability rather than the approval-gated level the prompt's phrasing might suggest.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Human manager decision does not weaken as model capability increases, but it approves only item and budget before any vendor quote exists, so it does not cover vendor identity or bank details.

controls.name: Prompt instruction restricting payment to approved vendor list
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model to check vendor identity against the list and never instructs it to validate that bank details match the known vendor's account. A more capable model may follow the letter of the instruction (correct vendor name) while still using attacker-supplied bank details.

controls.name: SSO authentication for purchase request submission
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by enterprise identity infrastructure outside the model; does not weaken with model capability.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of vendor bank details against a vetted vendor record
Human approval gate on payment delegation showing recipient and bank details
Signed and pinned payments-agent card with mutual authentication
Per-transaction scoped credential bound to approved amount and recipient
Spend and rate cap on payment delegation
Tamper-evident audit record linking approval, chosen vendor/bank details, and executed payment

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7) / confused deputy (TC4): untrusted vendor quote sets payment destination that bypasses the manager's approval scope

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled vendor quote email supplies fraudulent bank details, potentially impersonating an approved vendor's name.

Orchestrator checks the vendor name/domain against the approved vendor list; this validates vendor identity but not the bank account, so a spoofed-identity quote with different bank details still passes.
Orchestrator hands the chosen quote's bank details to payments-agent for payment, per the prompt's instruction to use the bank details from the chosen quote.
payments-agent trusts the task because it carries the orchestrator's bearer token, and pays the bank details in the task with no independent verification.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string on procurement-orchestrator changes, or median steps/runtime per purchasing task rises, without a new bank-detail verification or payment-specific approval control being added.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to 'Use the bank details from the chosen quote,' giving externally supplied content direct control over the payment destination.
Prompt claims 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' asserting a downstream safety control.

The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so the approval never covers the actual vendor or bank details paid.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, contradicting the prompt's claim that it performs remaining checks.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company, making in.vendor_quote an untrusted, externally controlled source.

recommendations.action: Verify vendor bank account details against an independently vetted vendor record (not the inbound quote) before executing payment; reject or hold when bank details differ from the vendor's known account.

Extend the manager approval gate (or add a second gate) to cover the specific vendor and bank details actually used for payment, and propagate that approval context to payments-agent so it can verify authorization before paying.
Scope the orchestrator-to-payments-agent credential and/or payment task to a specific approved amount and recipient, and add a spend/rate cap on cap.delegate_payment.
Record a tamper-evident audit trail that ties the manager's approval, the selected vendor quote, and the executed payment together for attribution.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card enables impersonation or silent redefinition of the payment tool (ASI04/ASI07)

forecast.watch_signal: New A2A agent card entries added without signature/pinning, or the payments-agent endpoint/card changes without an accompanying identity-verification control.

evidence.observation: The agent card declares only a bearer authentication scheme, with no signature or identity binding shown.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned, so its declared skills and endpoint can change or be spoofed without detection.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent card (and its tool/skill definitions) and verify peer identity (for example mTLS or signed identity) before trusting it at startup and on each use.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the orchestrator authenticates itself upstream or whether its own bearer token could be stolen or replayed elsewhere.
No capability of action configure targets the orchestrator's own config, prompt, or tools; it has no declared self-modification capability.
Artifacts do not describe what purchase or budget data the orchestrator discloses back to vendors during quoting.
Artifacts do not describe payments-agent's logging or storage of bank details after executing payment.
Artifacts confirm SSO authentication but do not describe whether purchase requests are logged with attributable employee identity.
Artifacts do not state whether inbound vendor email is authenticated via SPF, DKIM, or DMARC checks.
Artifacts do not describe what internal information is sent to vendors when requesting quotes.
Artifacts do not describe rate limiting or volume handling for inbound vendor quote emails.
Transport encryption is implied by the https URL but payload handling and logging of bank details in transit are not described.
Artifacts do not describe storage or integrity protections applied to the approval record itself.
Artifacts do not describe who can read the approval record or its access controls.
Artifacts do not describe availability protections for the approval record store.
No capability or input in the artifacts writes to the approved vendor list, and its integrity protections are not described.
Artifacts do not describe read access controls or sensitivity of the approved vendor list contents.
Artifacts provide no information on read volume or availability safeguards for the vendor list store.

rating.rationale: The dominant path is a business-email-compromise style authority-laundering attack: an externally supplied vendor quote (untrusted) determines the bank details used for an irreversible, delegated payment (S3), while the only human approval in the design authorizes budget and item before any quote exists and is never propagated to payments-agent, so it gives no credit on this path. The lone preventive control is a behavioral vendor-name check that does not validate bank details, holding residual at high; removing it under a model upgrade or longer task horizon returns the finding to critical. A secondary property finding on the unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card contributes an independent high-severity identity risk (impersonation or silent redefinition of the pay_vendor skill) that does not depend on the vendor-quote path and is capped at high per rubric 5a.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, agent card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agents.

No A2A traffic captures, logs, or approval-system configuration were provided; approval volume, inbound email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) status, and transport encryption details for the A2A call are recorded as not assessed rather than observed.
The approved vendor list's content and write-access controls were not provided, limiting confidence in how strongly the vendor-name check actually constrains vendor impersonation.
